evidence_quotes: Forty-five notable earthquakes (M4.0–M5.7) rattled the globe over the past 30 days
Tobelo, Indonesia was the busiest hotspot, recording 8 events
February 3 was the most active single day, logging 4 earthquakes
a shallow (5.7 km deep) M5.7 near the Kermadec Islands on February 8
Mohr, Iran recorded 3 events in the period
a deep M5.7 on February 14 and a shallow M5.3 on February 4
criticisms: The report describes the Tobelo M5.7 on February 14 as 'deep' — the digest shows depth_km of 152.9, which is indeed deep (>70 km), so this is accurate. No issue.
The report describes the Kermadec Islands M5.7 on February 8 as 'shallow (5.7 km deep)' — the digest confirms depth_km of 5.7, so this is accurate.

The report says 'nearly one in five earthquakes in the dataset' for Tobelo's 8 events out of 45 — 8/45 ≈ 17.8%, which is close to but not quite 'one in five' (20%). This is a minor rounding/framing imprecision but not a fabrication.

The report states 'Activity spanned six major zones: Indonesia, the Mariana Islands, Russia's Kuril Islands, Iran, Alaska, and the broader Pacific island chains' — all of these are supported by the digest's top_regions and sample_events. No invented locations.

The report says 'a shallow M5.3 on February 4' for Tobelo — the digest shows a 2026-02-04 event at '40 km E of Tobelo, Indonesia' with magnitude 5.3 and depth 21.4 km. Calling 21.4 km 'shallow' is a reasonable seismological characterization (shallow is typically <70 km), so this is acceptable.
The claim that 'February 3 was the most active single day, logging 4 earthquakes' is supported by the daily_counts showing 2026-02-03: 4, which is the highest single-day count in the digest.
